summary: Former fire tower site in Boone County, entered in the register in 2017 and listed as gone. No source describes what remains at the site today.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no source describes what remains.

events.note: Entered in the register as US 1662

evidence.supports: register name Piney Knob Tower Site

evidence.quote: Piney Knob Boone 37.98203 -81.90875 Tower Gone FFLOS US 1662, WV 53

evidence.supports: agency is West Virginia Division of Forestry
towers staffed about eight to fourteen weeks each spring and fall
evidence.quote: Towers were staffed for a period of about eight to 14 weeks each spring and fall when fires were most apt to occur.

evidence.supports: state towers phased out; last closed end of 1990 fall season
evidence.quote: State operated towers were gradually phased out with the last remaining ones permanently closed at the end of the 1990 fall fire season.

sources.title: Piney Knob Tower Site, Former Fire Lookout Sites Register
West Virginia Fire Towers, Alphabetical List
Robert Beanblossom: Fire towers had long, colorful history in WV

notes_for_editor: Thinnest of the three. No source gives a build date, staffing, a closure date or a description of the site. The story's statewide sentences (cite 4, Beanblossom op-ed) describe West Virginia towers in general and are not about this tower; a human may want to cut them. Agency comes only from the eastern lookouts page header (cite 3); the register page names no administrator. Record elevation 598.9 m agrees with the register's 599 m.
